claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud instance as a state backend.
The PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API on the self-hosted Pulumi API service.
An example valid value for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable is `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`.
When the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable is unset on the self-hosted API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves the PULUMI_API_DOMAIN environment variable's domain.
Using a separate domain for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN keeps the Terraform-compatible API distinct from the Pulumi API.
It is not required to use a separate domain for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN; it can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN if a second DNS record is not desired.

In Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, in the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command, and in the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name, the self-hosted PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value should be used wherever the state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com`.
The state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as an example domain.
